proposal.description: The ramp branch is gated off once SS_done is set, so the last S_SS clock after the ramp finishes falls through to the idle reset branch.
proposal.reason: The supervisor's state register leaves S_SS one clock after SS_done rises, so ss_active is still high on that clock. With this fault the ceiling drops back to MIN_ON_CNT and SS_done clears just as S_RUN starts, so S_RUN runs with the floor ceiling and SS_done low instead of holding the reached max_on_limit.

proposal.description: The at-target clamp is applied only while SS_done is still low, as if finishing the ramp needed acting on only once, so on the last S_SS clock after done the step branch is reachable again.
proposal.reason: Take a ramp finished by the clamp branch rather than by a step: max_on_limit equal to the floor, or lowered mid-ramp. If the following clock, still in S_SS, is a PWM falling edge at the end of a step window (every falling edge when cycles_per_step=1), the ceiling steps to max_on_limit+1. It is then held there through S_RUN, above the limit.

before: // Hold: ceiling and SS_done keep their values for all of S_RUN.
after: // Hold: ceiling and SS_done keep their values for all of S_RUN.
proposal.description: In S_RUN the digital ceiling is opened to full scale, leaving only the analog duty clamp, instead of holding the ceiling the ramp reached as a backstop.
proposal.reason: On the first clock of S_RUN max_on_counts jumps from max_on_limit to all-ones and stays there for the whole run. pwm_mask then no longer limits on-time to the programmed maximum while regulating.
